title: Robustness across conditions
outcome: Explain robustness across conditions using the records and boundaries of this fictional investigation.
scenario: Check robustness across conditions. A fixed classifier is tested separately on indoor and shaded outdoor cases.
given: Indoor 7/8 correct; outdoor 3/8 correct. The rubric and frozen model are unchanged.

steps.label: Name both slices
steps.detail: Each condition has eight labelled cases.

steps.label: Bound robustness
steps.detail: The large observed gap motivates investigation rather than claiming condition independence.

explanation: Robustness asks whether behaviour survives relevant changes in conditions. A total score can hide a weak slice; keep the scenario and denominator visible.

counterfactual.prediction: The arithmetic is correct, but the condition gap becomes hidden.
counterfactual.reason: Combining records discards the slice distinction relevant to the deployment goal.

student_task: Calculate indoor, outdoor and combined rates. Which relevant weakness disappears from view when only the combined rate is reported?
teacher_answer: Each condition has eight labelled cases. Indoor is 87.5%; outdoor is 37.5%. The large observed gap motivates investigation rather than claiming condition independence. Changed case: The arithmetic is correct, but the condition gap becomes hidden. Combining records discards the slice distinction relevant to the deployment goal.
project_evidence: For the Reproducible AI Research Study, retain an annotated worked trace and the changed-case reasoning. Connect the claim to its records, units and assumptions so another investigator can challenge or reproduce it.
limits: Eight cases per slice do not establish stable population rates or the reason for the difference.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice distinct from the reserved independent case. No invented significance, real experiment execution or pupil outcome is asserted.
